analysis:
Examined the head ClusterService.swift tail (lines 1340-1536), the ClusterPlacementFlow.swift base/head/patch (decide, lines 311-333 head), and the ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.swift patch (discoveryMode, head 39-48). I found no concrete regression.

Changes: (1) ClusterPlacementFlow now computes `assistant` once, passes `tensorAssistant:` into `ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine`, and passes `assistant?.policy` to synthesize unchanged. This only affects the narration line about public traffic. It is a tightening: a Qwen speculative-assistant TP setup is described as not offered to public traffic. The actual enforcement (`ClusterConfiguration.tensorAssistantServesLocally`, the leader refusing coordinator approval) lives in files not supplied here. I could not verify it, but nothing in the supplied diff relaxes it.
(2) `discoveryMode(_:coordinator:)` maps auto to off when the setup serves through the coordinator. This reduces the assistant's exposure. Explicit `on` is preserved and is documented as refused downstream; that refusal is outside the evidence.
(3) ClusterService adds an injectable `environment` (default nil, so the process environment) and `partEnvironment`, which redirects the heartbeat file env var to a part-specific path. Spawned parts still inherit the full parent environment as before. The log file is created 0600. The change is availability-oriented (the liveness guard no longer sees another pid's beats) and adds no new trust boundary. The `environment` parameter is an internal init, not a public API.

Related threats (T-053/T-054 and TB-011) are not weakened by this diff. Open questions for integration: whether `publicTrafficLine` actually accepts the new `tensorAssistant` parameter (not shown; it is a compile-level matter), and whether the coordinator approval refusal for assistant setups is enforced at the call sites. Both are outside the supplied evidence, so I recorded them as unverified rather than as findings.
